x: Round they came for the second time with Bobby Reid of Birchfield hanging on to Jack Holden's shoulder, and Len Herbert had kept his position and looked a certainty for International honours.
Len Herbert went off just in front of Bobby Reid for the final leg, and they turned the last corner still together, but Len got in front with a fine finishing burst.

Birchfield had a good four running for them and although Vic Blowfield gave us the lead on the first leg, which Ted Stimpson maintained on the second stage, Bill Lucas had to give way to Reeves of Birchfield and Bobby Reid went off with a good lead from George Lucas for the last lap.
The next leg to Hickstead, about six miles, is considered as perhaps the stiffest and most important, and Vernon Blowfield was up against Bobby Reid, "Sidney" and Stan Belton (Surrey).
The Midland at Great Barr the same day went to the veteran performer Bobby Reid of Birchfield by only a second from team mate Ted Dalton with their club comfortably taking the team title.
